sections.overview: Dichomeris alacella is a small gelechiid moth known in Britain as the Lichen Sober.
sections.identification: Its pointed forewings have pale patches beyond three dark stigmata, with pale-tipped dark labial palps; the wingspan is about 13–14 mm.
sections.habitat: It is associated with woodland, especially mature broad-leaved trees and possibly ancient broad-leaved woods; long-established fruit trees may also host larval signs.
sections.diet: The larva has been reported feeding on mosses and lichens on trunks and fences; a Dutch observation found one beneath a lichen on an oak branch.
sections.behavior: Adults rest on tree trunks by day. At night, they come to artificial lights.
sections.reproduction: Adults fly mainly in July and August; the early stages remain poorly described.
sections.ecology: Its larval food is associated with bark surfaces rather than living foliage, linking the moth to lichens and mosses on mature woody substrates.
sections.conservation: The British recording scheme calls it nationally scarce but notes a recent increase in records; this regional trend should not be treated as a global assessment.
